lesson.title: Sí or No? A Silly Question Game with Sol
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol has a silly game today! Sol asks a question, and you give a thumbs up for [[sí]] (yes) or a thumbs down for [[no]] (no).
Listen for the question: ¿Es un perro? 🐶 (Is that a dog?) Thumbs up and say sí, or thumbs down and say no!
Try another one: ¿Es un pez? 🐟 (Is that a fish?) Thumbs up and say sí, or thumbs down and say no!
You answered with sí and no — just like a real conversation! Tomorrow is our biggest day yet: a greeting circle with Sol and all your favorite words.

questions.q: Grown-up, read aloud: 🐶 ¿Es un perro? (Is this a dog?)
Grown-up, read aloud: 🐟 ¿Es un perro? (Is this a dog?)
questions.explanation: ¡No! That is a fish, not a dog.

questions.q: Grown-up, read aloud: 🌞 ¿Es de noche? (Is it night?)
questions.explanation: ¡No! The sun means it's daytime — buenos días!

questions.q: Grown-up, read aloud: 🌙 ¿Es de noche? (Is it night?)
questions.explanation: ¡Sí! The moon means it's nighttime — buenas noches!

objectives: Answer a simple either/or question with sí (yes) or no (no), paired with a thumbs up/down gesture
Distinguish sí from no by sound and gesture in a playful question game
materialsNeeded: A few animal pictures or toys already at home (a dog, a fish, a cat — whatever you have)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Explain the game: Sol will ask silly yes-or-no questions about pictures, and your child answers with a thumbs up (sí) or thumbs down (no) — say the words together too.
2. Ask 2-3 silly questions aloud yourself first, e.g. 'Is a fish a dog? ¿Es un perro?' while pointing at a picture of a fish, letting your child answer sí or no with thumbs and words.
3. Take turns — let your child make up a silly question for you to answer!
4. Move to the on-screen sí/no activity: since your child likely can't read yet, read each question aloud to them, and let them choose sí or no on the screen while also giving a thumbs signal.
5. Complete the worksheet the same way — read each line aloud.
6. Close by asking: 'What do we say when the answer is yes? When it's no?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: use only real objects in the room for the questions ('Is this a table? ¿Es una mesa?') so the answer is obvious and confidence-building
Ready for more: let your child ask Sol the silly questions instead of just answering them
The sillier the question, the better — asking something wrong on purpose ('¿Es un perro?' while pointing at a fish) makes the no answer fun instead of stressful
teacherGuide.answerKey: Read each question aloud with your child: 1. 'Is this a dog?' pointing at a dog picture — sí. 2. 'Is this a dog?' pointing at a fish picture — no. Any silly variation you invent follows the same pattern: sí if it matches the picture, no if it doesn't.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Targets sí/no as essential building blocks of Interpersonal Communication (WA-WL-2015.1.1) through a listening-and-gesture game adapted for read-aloud delivery, since the platform has no audio/TTS infrastructure yet for a true listening activity (open decision, expansion-plan-2026-09.md §12.9) — the parent's voice stands in for the recording, the same accommodation used in the grade-6 checkpoint's Day 4.

generationData.instructions: Read each line aloud to your child and have them answer with a thumbs up (sí) or thumbs down (no).

rows.problem: Read aloud: '¿Es un perro?' while pointing at a picture of a dog. Have your child give a thumbs up and say sí.
Read aloud: '¿Es un perro?' while pointing at a picture of a fish. Have your child give a thumbs down and say no.
